title: Estate lifecycle & governance schema absent: no draft/publish/verify/deactivate/transfer/tz/branding
expected: Estate has draft state, publish, verification, deactivation, ownership transfer, timezone, branding
actual: CLOSED by Phase 2.3 on 2026-10-27. The status machine from caef65516 (pending -> verify -> active -> suspend -> reactivate -> close, review queue, actor-attributed status changes, legal hold) is now asserted over HTTP and against the live database rather than only by Go tests (EXEC-ESTA-026: 140 PASS / 0 FAIL; EXEC-ESTA-025: 10 PASS / 0 FAIL), and everything the PARTIAL note listed as absent has been built: estates.timezone validated against pg_timezone_names by trigger and by constraint; estates.branding (four allow-listed keys, #rrggbb, http(s), 4 KB) and estates.notice (2000 runes, counted in characters not bytes); estates.duplicate_suspected with normalised (name,address) detection that holds a twin in the review queue instead of publishing it; estate_config_revisions written by an AFTER trigger under pg_advisory_xact_lock with previous_value, newest-first, and no rows for untouched columns; estate_owner_transfers with a one-pending partial unique and a single SECURITY DEFINER writer so ownership moves only on the incoming owner's accept. Deliberate remaining shape, recorded so it is not mistaken for an oversight: the pre-publication state is 'pending' (an application in the platform queue), not a separately editable draft; a handover transfers the estate, not individual units; branding and timezone are stored, validated and served but no client renders them and no estate code reads the zone for computation; and the surface sits behind FEATURE_ESTATE_LIFECYCLE_ENABLED / FEATURE_ESTATE_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED, both false by default.
root_cause: Feature set never modeled; needs additive migrations (deferred to consolidation)

title: Estate role model is binary (resident|estate_admin): no finance/gate/election/facility/auditor/temporary delegations
expected: Scoped delegated roles with least privilege and expiring assignments
actual: PARTIAL as of 554173ae0: estate_staff_grants gives 7 expiring, revocable, admin-delegated roles and the gate path is genuinely least-privilege (assertGate fail-closed; EST-UAT-0056/0061/0068 now PASS via EXEC-ESTA-014). Updated 2026-10-27 (Phase 2.3): EST-UAT-0028 is closed — estate_invite_codes.role (migration 20271099000050) lets an admin mint a manager code, an omitted role defaults to resident, a resident code cannot demote a sitting owner and grants no admin surface, proven live in EXEC-ESTA-025/026. Still open: finance_officer/election_officer/facility_officer/meeting_secretary/auditor are grantable but consulted by no action path (EXEC-ESTA-016), enforcement sits behind FEATURE_ESTATE_GUARD_GRANTS which defaults false, and estate_residents.role is still the binary resident|estate_admin super-role enum — deliberately, because the invite CHECK is bounded by estate_residents_role_check and widening it is a schema-plus-service change, not an invite change
root_cause: Role enum CHECK constraint limits the model; widening needs schema + service changes

title: Merchant onboarding lacks withdraw/suspend/reactivate; resubmit only from NEEDS_MORE_INFO
expected: Withdrawal, suspension, reactivation and linked resubmission lifecycle
actual: No withdraw or suspend/reactivate endpoints; Resubmit only accepts NEEDS_MORE_INFO, rejected app starts a new case
root_cause: Lifecycle subset implemented (draft/submit/review/approve/reject/info/escalate)

title: Account deletion had no liability hold
expected: Closure follows hold policy and does not orphan financial records
actual: Account soft-deleted immediately regardless of unpaid invoices
root_cause: No liability check before delete

title: Vendor payout account stored unverified
expected: Invalid account rejected; verified account approved for settlement only
actual: bank_account blob persisted without any account-name/bank-code verification
root_cause: No provider account-resolution integration on the estate vendor path

title: Occupancy overlap, effective-date gating and vacant-unit fee policy not enforced
expected: Overlaps rejected; access follows effective dates; fees follow vacant rules
actual: Found live on 2026-10-21 and fixed in Phase 2.4, proved on 2026-10-27 (EXEC-ESTA-029 sections 4, 4d, 6d, 7, 8, 9 and 11, plus TestLiveDB_Occupancy_*): every occupancy change now goes through the single admitting writer estate_occupancy_admit, which enforces capacity and the one-tenant rule in the same statement that marks the unit, with estate_occupancy_release closing it; gate access and dues follow the occupancy's effective dates (an out-of-term occupant is refused, a NULL window is unrestricted), and a charge for a vacant or out-of-term unit is 409 unless the estate admin files a reason-backed written override. The policy gaps the case left open were settled by product decision: vacant units are exempt (EST-UAT-0048), capacity defaults to 6 with CHECK > 0 under one owner with many tenants allowed off (EST-UAT-0044), and NULL means unrestricted for both access and dues (EST-UAT-0045).
root_cause: Rules engine not modeled — approval wrote the occupancy row directly with no capacity, overlap, effective-date or fee-policy check in the path

title: No estate/building bulk import (only visitor CSV)
expected: Estate settings/buildings importable with row-level validation
actual: No estate or building import endpoint exists
root_cause: Feature never built

title: QR payload unsigned; no offline cached-credential admission policy

title: Pass sharing is a stub: no SMS/push delivery to visitor phone
expected: Correct redacted invite delivered once or controlled retry logged
actual: 204 intent endpoint; nothing is sent to the visitor

expected: Out-of-policy code not issued; over-quota denied/escalated
actual: Any window length and unlimited passes per resident accepted
root_cause: No policy read/enforcement in the create path

title: No per-gate assignment, supervisor-override permission, identity check, or device binding at the gate
expected: Gate-specific passes honored; overrides require authorized role + reason; unenrolled devices denied
actual: Live-confirmed 2026-10-26 on the shipped surface (EXEC-ESTA-022): a plain resident with NO estate_staff_grants row opened POST /api/v1/visitor/gate/session (201), read gate/expected (200) and admitted a visitor via gate/approve (200) - the BFF authorises gate work by estate membership only. On the Go stack the guard admit path is fail-closed (estate_staff_grants + assertGate -> ErrNotMember/ErrInsufficientRole/ErrAccountBanned/ErrAccountDeleted, proven by the live-DB suite in EXEC-ESTA-014 and over HTTP in EXEC-ESTA-017) but only behind FEATURE_ESTATE_GUARD_GRANTS, which defaults to false (EXEC-ESTA-018). Still open in both stacks: no code.gate assignment, no supervisor-override permission for walk-in, no identity check, no device enrolment
root_cause: Gate-policy model not designed (schema gaps: code.gate, device registry, supervisor role)

title: Resident real-time approval flow absent (approve/decline/timeout)
expected: Entry permitted only after resident approval; decline and timeout enforced
actual: Live-confirmed 2026-10-26 (EXEC-ESTA-022): a pass requested with requireHostApproval:true is stored with require_host_approval = f because the codes insert list in frontend-web/app/api/v1/visitor/codes/route.ts omits the column, and a guard then admitted that pass (200) with no host decision - the flag is neither persisted nor consulted on the shipped path. The Go service does model it end to end (visitor_arrival_requests pending/approved/declined, RequestArrival/DecideArrival routes, admission denied until approval, single-use approvals, 15-min TTL; EXEC-ESTA-014) but that stack is not what mobile calls, and nothing writes status='timeout' for a request the host never answers
root_cause: Approval workflow not modeled (no pending-approval status on codes/visits)

title: No visitor PII retention/purge policy
expected: PII hidden/purged/anonymized after retention threshold
actual: Codes expire but visitor name/phone/plate persist forever
root_cause: Retention job only flips status; no anonymization step

title: Estate directory enumerable by any authenticated user while FEATURE_ESTATE_GUARD_GRANTS is at its default
expected: Discovery is membership-scoped (or explicitly scoped public-by-consent) regardless of flag state
actual: Confirmed live on :8094 with the flag unset: GET /api/finance/estate?limit=50 as a user with no membership returns the full row set (id, name, admin_id, created_at); the same call on :8093 with the flag on returns {"data":null}. listAllEstates() is the documented pre-#876 behaviour, so the fail-closed discovery rule only exists when a non-default flag is turned on
root_cause: Caller-scoping of estate discovery was coupled to the guard-grants flag instead of being its own always-on rule

title: Gate lookup id-prefix branch can never match and the failure is reported as not-found
expected: The documented lookup works by numeric_code or by id prefix, and a broken query is distinguishable from an unknown code
actual: Live (EXEC-ESTA-022): lookup?code=<first 8 chars of an issued pass id> answers 200 {"found":false}. The id-prefix filter is a PostgREST 404 with sqlcode 42883 operator does not exist: uuid ~~* unknown (same error raised directly in psql against supabase_db_spotlight), and the route destructures only { data: rows }, discarding error, so the operator sees 'not found' for a query that never ran
root_cause: visitor_access_codes.id is a uuid column, so ILIKE needs a cast (id::text ilike ...); the swallowed Supabase error converts a broken query into a false negative

title: CSV pass import reports no per-row outcome, so malformed rows vanish silently
expected: Import responds with the accepted count plus which rows were skipped and why (or fails the batch)
actual: Live (EXEC-ESTA-021): a 3-row CSV whose last line is malformed returns 201 {"imported":2}; nothing tells the operator a row was dropped. The insert is also one batch, so a single bad value would reject every row while the success path implies partial acceptance
root_cause: rows are filtered on required fields before insert and the response only counts inserted rows

title: The BFF estate write gate (fc6fd64f7) shipped without fixture support, silently invalidating 23 visitor/estate specs
expected: A behaviour change lands with the fixtures it depends on, so a red suite is visible in the commit that caused it rather than five days later
actual: fc6fd64f7 added assertEstateWritable, which answers 423 unless estates.status='active', while those four specs create no estates row at all: 23 specs went red and the 20 estate-a cases whose evidence cites them silently lost their proof from 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-26. Repaired 2026-10-26 by seeding status='active' into the fixtures and adding 2 negative 423 specs (EXEC-ESTA-013 now reports 12 files / 116 tests green); the repair is in the working tree and committed in c4c69e0cd (2026-10-27). Production was never locked out — estates.status is NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' — so this is a test-integrity/ledger defect, not a user-facing one
root_cause: The write gate was landed without running the suite that exercises it, and the fixtures predated the column

title: POST /estate accepted a name made of spaces and queued a live estate
expected: A missing or blank estate name is refused with 400 before anything is stored
actual: Found live on 2026-10-27 (EXEC-ESTA-026 first run): {'name':'   '} returned 201 and created a real estate held in the platform review queue; a padded name was stored untrimmed and slipped past the duplicate lookup
root_cause: Gin's binding:'required,min=2' counts characters, so three spaces satisfy it, and nothing re-checked the value in the service before the INSERT. Fixed in CreateEstate: trim, require at least 2 runes, refuse with the new ErrEstateNameRequired sentinel mapped to 400, store the trimmed name and use it for estateDuplicateLookup. The estate the first run created (43543a7e-7ae9-4c7a-9707-952d74812406) was closed over the real reject transition rather than deleted out of the ledger.

title: Estate governance routes answered caller mistakes with 500 instead of 400
expected: A bad query parameter, an out-of-range field or an impossible target is a refused request (400) with the reason, not a server failure (500)
actual: Found live on 2026-10-27 (EXEC-ESTA-026 first run and the spot checks that followed it): an over-length resident notice, an unknown ?column= on /admin/config/history, an unknown ?status= on /owner-transfers, an unparseable or self to_user_id on POST /owner-transfer and an unknown timezone on POST /estate each returned 500
root_cause: The service returned bare fmt.Errorf values and parse errors, and the httperr rule table had no 400 bucket for them. Fixed with sentinels — ErrNoticeTooLong, ErrInvalidConfigColumn, ErrInvalidTransferFilter, ErrInvalidTransferTargetUser, ErrOwnerTransferToSelf, ErrInvalidTimezone, ErrEstateNameRequired — mapped to http.StatusBadRequest in profile_handler.go and handler.go; the live-DB tests now assert with errors.Is rather than matching message text.

title: Ownership claims accepted a unit id from another estate (cross-estate IDOR)
expected: A unit id that does not belong to the estate in the path is refused, and no other estate's unit can be claimed into a review queue
actual: Found while building the M03 surface: the service took no estate id at all — ClaimOwnership(ctx, propertyID, userID, docURL) — so a member of estate A could queue an ownership claim against estate B's unit and only B's admin could decide it. Fixed and proved live: EXEC-ESTA-029 section 14 (a second estate's unit id answers 404 on the claim, occupancy-proof, tenancy and vehicle routes) and TestLiveDB_Occupancy_* on the live database
root_cause: The write trusted a caller-supplied id as a capability instead of re-deriving the estate from it

title: Vehicle verification updated another estate's plate (cross-estate IDOR)
expected: An estate admin can only set the verified flag on a vehicle registered to a member of their own estate
actual: Found while building the M03 surface: the UPDATE matched resident_vehicles by id alone, so any estate admin who passed another estate's vehicle id flipped verified/verified_by on it. Fixed by joining through estate_residents on the path estate and reporting ErrVehicleNotFound (404) when nothing matches; proved by EXEC-ESTA-029 section 14 and TestLiveDB_Occupancy_CrossEstateVehicleVerification, which also shows the verdict is revoked when the document behind it is replaced
root_cause: The writer scoped by actor role but not by the row's estate

title: A property_type outside the column domain returned 500
expected: An unknown unit type is a refused request (400) naming the field, with the allowed values in the message
actual: Found live on 2026-10-27 (EXEC-ESTA-029 first run): POST /properties with a type the estate_properties CHECK does not allow returned 500 and the unit id never came back, which cascaded through the rest of the lane. Fixed by modeling the domain once in Go (PropertyTypes = apartment|house|commercial|land|other, shared by create, update and the bulk import), trimming the value before the check and mapping ErrInvalidPropertyType to 400; the update route now enforces the same rule the create route does
root_cause: The database owned the domain and the service had no equivalent, so a rejected value surfaced as a driver error

title: A unit's landlord cannot read that unit's occupancy register
expected: The owner of a unit should see who occupies it, scoped to that unit
actual: Proved as current behaviour rather than assumed: ListOccupancies scopes every non-admin to o.user_id = actor for the module's personal-data rule, so a landlord who just approved a tenancy reads only their own rows (asserted in TestLiveDB_Occupancy_TenancyApprovalAdmitsWithoutDemotion and EXEC-ESTA-029 sections 5 and 6c). The refusal is consistent and it is not an authorisation leak — but the unit owner's own register is unreachable over the API today
root_cause: The register was built as the estate's personal-data view, with no unit-owner branch between the admin's whole-register read and the member's own-rows read

title: Approving a tenancy demoted the estate's own admin
expected: Deciding a tenancy request must never change a third party's estate role
actual: Found while building the M03 surface: the old approval wrote the tenant onto the unit and then upserted a residency with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET role='resident', so when the tenant was an estate_admin the approving landlord demoted that admin mid-transaction and the estate lost its administrator to a tenancy it had just granted. Fixed by routing approval through the single admitting writer (estate_occupancy_admit), which is promotion-only and never revives a banned or deleted membership; proved live by EXEC-ESTA-029 section 11 (the admin tenant is still on /admin/residents?role=estate_admin, still administers units and still reads the claim queue) and TestLiveDB_Occupancy_TenancyApprovalAdmitsWithoutDemotion
root_cause: A side effect of the approval re-used the membership upsert, and that upsert treated every residency write as a role assignment

title: Approving an empty occupancy declaration returned 500
expected: Marking a declaration verified when no document is on record is a refused decision (409) that says there is nothing to read
actual: Found while building the proof review route: the service raised ErrProofNeedsDocument to stop a reviewer clearing a queue without reading anything, but the error was not in the HTTP rule table, so the refusal rendered as 500. Mapped to 409 and asserted live (EXEC-ESTA-029 section 10o: a member who declared a label and filed no document gets 409 'there is no document on record to verify', while an id the estate holds no registration for is 404)
root_cause: A sentinel added with the verification rule was not carried into the status-code table alongside it

title: The dues routes answered 403 for every service error
expected: An estate rule that refuses a charge is 409, a caller mistake is 400, and 403 means the caller lacked the role
actual: Found live on 2026-10-27: both dues handlers hard-coded http.StatusForbidden for any error from the service, so the vacant-unit exemption, the out-of-term exemption, an override without a reason and a non-positive amount all reported a permission failure — an operator could not tell 'you may not' from 'this charge may not exist'. Fixed by giving them the shared writeOccupancyError rule table; the exemptions now read 409 with the reason and amount mistakes stay 400 naming the field (EXEC-ESTA-029 sections 6d, 7 and 8)
root_cause: The handlers predated the occupancy error map and carried their own status code

title: Malformed unit and claim ids on the M03 write routes returned 500
file_paths: backend/internal/estate/handler.go (validUUIDParam on ClaimOwnership, ReviewOwnershipClaim, CreateTenancyRequest, ReviewTenancyRequest, SetOccupancyStatus, ArchiveProperty)
expected: A syntactically invalid id is refused at the edge with 400 and never reaches the database
actual: Found live on 2026-10-27: those routes passed c.Param values straight into uuid-typed queries, so 'not-a-uuid' produced a driver error and a 500 while a real typo looked like a server outage. Fixed by adding the shape check to every M03 write route (and the tenancy review route), asserted with 400 in EXEC-ESTA-029 sections 2b, 5b and 10
root_cause: The shape check was introduced with the new occupancy handlers (occupancy_handler.go); the claim, tenancy, status and archive routes are older handlers in handler.go and were written before it existed

title: An unknown status filter on the ownership-claims queue returned an empty 200
expected: A filter value the queue cannot hold is a 400 listing the three allowed statuses
actual: Found while making the claim queue readable (the table could be written and reviewed by id but never listed): a typo in ?status= silently selected nothing, so a reviewer's screen would read 'nothing to review' when the filter was simply wrong. Fixed by validating against pending|approved|rejected and mapping ErrInvalidClaimFilter to 400 (EXEC-ESTA-029 section 10)
root_cause: The status parameter was applied as a WHERE clause without consulting the column's own CHECK set

title: Filing a tenancy request discloses the unit's landlord id to a caller who is not a member
expected: A filing that resolves the unit's real owner should not echo that owner's user id back to a non-member
actual: Proved live on 2026-10-27 (EXEC-ESTA-029 section 14): CreateTenancyRequest correctly ignores the body's landlord_id and binds the request to the unit's real owner — but the 201 response returns the resolved landlord_id, and filing needs no estate membership, so an authenticated outsider can read a member id out of another estate's unit. The same run proves no access is gained (that outsider is 403 on the estate's unit list). Left RECORDED: the remedy is a response-trimming decision (return the request id and status only, or require membership to file), which is the product owner's call rather than a security default
root_cause: The request row is built server-side from the unit and returned whole, and the route has no membership assert to limit who sees that echo

title: A refused estate write leaves no trace in the audit log
file_paths: backend/internal/estate/property_mgmt.go (UpdateProperty, AssignLandlord/AssignTenant); backend/internal/estate/occupancy.go (the role and term asserts); backend/internal/estate/handler.go
expected: EST-UAT-0050 asks that an unauthorized edit be rejected AND logged: a refused write should record who tried, against what and why it was refused
actual: Proved as current behaviour rather than assumed on 2026-10-27: EXEC-ESTA-029 section 9 reads the audit log and finds the successful events (ESTATE_UNIT_OCCUPANT_ADMITTED / _RELEASED, INVOICE_VACANCY_OVERRIDE, INVOICE_TERM_OVERRIDE), while every refusal asserted in sections 2b, 5, 10, 12 and 14 answers 403/400 and writes nothing — the audit calls sit after the successful statement (s.audit / auditTx on the success path), so the estate cannot see an attempt trail for the very edits the case treats as security events
root_cause: The audit sink was built as a consequence of writes that succeeded; no refusal path was ever given a logging branch, and the role asserts return before reaching one
